step_by_step_reasoning: First, we identify the main user flow: User Devices initiate a rendering request via API Gateway, which forwards it to the Frontend Lambda. The Frontend Lambda splits requests and pushes tasks to a Request SQS Queue. Rendering EC2 Instances (managed inside an EC2 Auto Scaling Group) pull tasks from the SQS queue and immediately acknowledge via a Response SQS Queue, allowing the Frontend Lambda to quickly return a playlist link to the user. Next, we construct the rendering storage and playback flow: the EC2 Instances upload video segments to an S3 bucket, which serves as the origin for CloudFront to cache and stream back to the User Devices. Finally, we model the operational and scaling management flows described in the audio: 1) A custom scaling workflow where AWS Step Functions triggers a Scaling Lambda every 15 seconds, which evaluates engine metrics from CloudWatch and dynamically adjusts the EC2 Auto Scaling Group capacity. 2) A spot instance interruption handling workflow where CloudWatch Events notifies an Interruption Lambda of impending Spot terminations, triggering the Lambda to command the affected EC2 instance to drain its jobs and safely detaching it from the Auto Scaling Group.

graph.name: SundaySky Rendering as a Service (RAS) Architecture
graph.notes: Architectural representation of SundaySky's personalized video rendering engine using EC2 Spot instances, SQS queues, Step Functions scaling orchestration, and a custom spot instance interruption draining mechanism.

nodes.name: User Devices
nodes.notes: Initiates personalized rendering requests and plays back video segments.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Entry point for client devices, configured with usage plans and API keys to manage API load.

nodes.name: Frontend Lambda
nodes.notes: Validates requests, pushes tasks to SQS, and retrieves immediate responses to provide playlist links.

nodes.name: Request Queue
nodes.notes: Buffers the rendering tasks/instructions for the processing engines.

nodes.name: Response Queue
nodes.notes: Receives quick start acknowledgments from processing engines to complete the playlist link handshake.

nodes.name: Rendering EC2 Instances
nodes.notes: Diversified, multi-AZ spot instances that process rendering tasks and upload video chunks.

nodes.name: EC2 Auto Scaling
nodes.notes: Dynamically scales diversified instance types across multiple AZs to ensure cost efficiency and high availability.

nodes.name: S3 Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores rendered video segments uploaded by EC2 rendering engines.

nodes.name: CloudFront CDN
nodes.notes: Caches and serves video segments globally to client players.

nodes.name: Step Functions Orchestrator
nodes.notes: Triggers the custom scaling loop every 15 seconds to evaluate farm load.

nodes.name: Scaling Lambda
nodes.notes: Calculates required rendering capacity based on CloudWatch metrics and triggers ASG scaling changes.

nodes.name: CloudWatch Events / Metrics
nodes.notes: Hosts instance metrics and publishes spot interruption event notices.

nodes.name: Interruption Lambda
nodes.notes: Handles spot terminations by telling the targeted EC2 instance to drain rendering tasks and detaching it from the ASG.

edges.notes: User requests a personalized video stream.
Routes the API request to the Frontend Lambda.

Spot EC2 instances pull rendering jobs when they have spare capacity.

Frontend Lambda polls for fast response to get playlist details.
Returns playlist link back to the user device player.
Uploads generated video segments to S3 storage.
Device player requests segments via the CloudFront CDN endpoint.
CloudFront fetches missing or expired video segments from the S3 origin.
Triggers the scaling evaluator Lambda function every 15 seconds.
Queries custom engine metrics pushed from EC2 instances to CloudWatch.
Adjusts instance desired capacity on the Auto Scaling Group based on workload calculations.
Sends 2-minute spot instance termination notice event to the Interruption Handler.
Triggers EC2 API to stop pulling new jobs and finish rendering current work before timeout.
Detaches the terminating spot instance from the Auto Scaling Group dynamically.
